title: What this app supports
summary: An honest answer to what runs where, what keeps working without a connection, and where the character data comes from.

rows.android: On Android, install the app from its release page. It updates itself when a new version is out. It is not on Google Play, so your phone will ask you to allow the install once.
rows.iphone: On iPhone and iPad, open the site in Safari and add it to your home screen. That installed web app is the intended way to use this on iOS — there is no App Store version, and none is planned.
rows.computer: On a computer, open the site in any modern browser. Nothing to install.

rows.tested: The app is tested on all three major browser engines, not just one.
rows.engines: Chromium covers Chrome, Edge and Opera. Firefox is its own engine. WebKit is what Safari uses — and what every browser on iPhone uses, whichever one you install.
rows.reporting: If something looks wrong in your browser, it is worth reporting: a rendering problem on one engine is a real bug here, not something you are expected to work around.

rows.works: The character catalogue, both team builders, Captain Coverage, your saved teams and your boxes all keep working with no connection.
rows.needsConnection: Signing in, Google Drive sync and downloading a new version need a connection. Nothing else does.
rows.storage: Your teams and boxes are stored on this device, not on a server. Clearing the browser's site data deletes them - and on iPhone the browser can also clear them on its own if you have not opened the app for a long while. The app asks the browser to keep them, but cannot guarantee it, so export anything you would not want to lose.

permissions.title: What the Android app asks for

rows.internet: Internet — to load the character data and to sync if you sign in.
rows.installPackages: Install packages — only so the app can install its own update when you accept one. It is never used for anything else.
rows.nothingElse: Nothing else. No contacts, no location, no camera, no files beyond what you export yourself.

rows.source: Character data comes from the One Piece Treasure Cruise community database that the game's players maintain.
rows.freshness: It is rebuilt with every release, and a release goes out automatically when that database gains new characters.
rows.unofficial: This is a fan-made tool. It is not made by, endorsed by, or connected to Bandai Namco.
